summary.headline: Global Surfaces Q2 FY27 revenue rose 10.7% YoY to Rs 60 crore, EBITDA margin 2.17% on cost pressures; PAT loss Rs 5.4 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 60 crore, up 10.7% YoY but up only 8.4% sequentially per the call's wording (the transcript says "lower than 8.4%", which is ambiguous). EBITDA was Rs 1.3 crore (margin 2.17%) versus a Rs 3.6 crore loss a year ago and a 12.69% margin in Q1, as raw material costs rose 25-50% and imported-raw-material freight rose nearly fivefold. Loss after tax was Rs 5.4 crore against Rs 4.6 crore a year ago and near breakeven in Q1. H1 EBITDA doubled to Rs 9.6 crore with margin up 424 bps to 7.66%, but other income fell to Rs 1.8 crore from Rs 9.4 crore, leaving H1 loss after tax at Rs 5.3 crore.

segments.name: Engineered quartz (group)
segments.commentary: Engineered stone makes up about 98% of H1 revenue after the Bagru natural stone unit was discontinued effective 31 March 2026. Export accounts for about 96% of revenue and domestic about 4%.

segments.name: US (Global Surfaces Inc. / Superior Surfaces Inc.)
segments.commentary: Per a question on Roshni Mehta's note, US revenue was flat and the segment reached break-even; management did not dispute this in the answer, but no figures were given on the call.

segments.name: UAE (Global Surfaces FZE, Jebel Ali)
segments.commentary: Management said the UAE business makes cash profit, though an analyst cited a UAE loss of about Rs 57 million in Q2 vs Rs 31 million in Q1 on flat revenue. Management did not confirm these figures.

segments.name: India (Mahindra World City SEZ, Jaipur)
segments.commentary: Domestic brand launch via dealer network planned this quarter, with domestic dispatches from November 2026. About 70% of domestic-product output is to come from the India plant and 30-35% from UAE.

segments.name: Marquartz (patented/licensed product)
segments.commentary: Average selling price is about 20-30% above regular products, with capacity utilisation similar to the group average, and competition is lower given the patent.

guidance_outlook: Management said the near-term operating environment will remain challenging given US trade measures and regional geopolitics.
Margin recovery to ~12% depends on efficiency gains and cost normalisation; management said it is hard to say whether margins return to 12% if conditions persist.
Cost of raw materials expected to normalise within 1-2 months if geopolitical situation stabilises.
Revenue run rate of Rs 70-80 crore per quarter: management said realistically Q4 FY27, dependent on geopolitics.
Receivables expected to return to normal levels towards end of Q3 FY27 (turnaround of 90-150 days).
Conversion of loan to FZE equity (Rs 110-111 crore) approval done; process expected to take 2-3 months with immediate financial effect per management.
summary.management_tone: Management was candid but defensive on margins and pricing, repeatedly tying the outlook to geopolitical stabilisation. Answers on UAE losses, cash flow from payables and utilisation thresholds were vague or left unanswered, and some answers were approximate by management's own admission.
key_quotes: So, we are already at cash break-even. We are not making any cash losses in H1.
But if the situation remains to the present standard, it is difficult to say that whether it will get back to 12% or not.
So, once the geopolitical situation stabilizes, we are able to utilize our capacities in a better manner, we see the profitability increasing dramatically from here.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q2 EBITDA margin fall to about 2.2% from 12.7% in Q1, and will it recur in Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Q1 spillover of inventories sold at pre-war prices and higher input costs in Q2. Margin recovers if efficiency and costs are managed, but if conditions persist it is difficult to say whether margin returns to 12%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the raw material and freight cost has been passed to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Not much; most cost is absorbed. Only part of freight cost passed on via FOB terms and no selling price increases taken, attributed to Section 201 disruption. Price increases may follow once the market adjusts and if input costs keep rising.

qa_highlights.question: How much of price hike vs mix vs currency, and can prices be raised again?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost increase is about 10% on selling prices; timing of any further price hike depends on geopolitics and market acceptance. Costs should normalise within 1-2 months if geopolitics stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: What utilisation is needed to reach break-even, given H1 volume is about one-third of capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is at cash break-even with no cash losses in H1 and profitability should rise sharply once utilisation improves after geopolitical stabilisation. No utilisation threshold given.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the UAE loss rise to about Rs 57 million from Rs 31 million in Q1 on flat revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the UAE business is not making cash losses and is making a cash profit despite low utilisation. The specific loss figures were not addressed.

qa_highlights.question: When will revenue reach Rs 70-80 crore per quarter to aid operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is possible this quarter if geopolitics stabilise, but realistically Q4 FY27. H1 saw multiple raw material disruptions and production breakdowns.

qa_highlights.question: How much better are Marquartz prices and margins, and will volumes grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Marquartz ASP is about 20-30% above regular products, utilisation similar to group, competition lower due to patent. Volumes expected to rise but are constrained by raw material shortages.

qa_highlights.question: Why did India PBT deteriorate sharply from Q1 on lower revenue, and what will domestic sales add in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said domestic launch will lift India capacity utilisation, cut overhead per unit, and raise revenue; about 70% of domestic output from India plant and 30-35% from UAE. No India PBT figures given.

qa_highlights.question: Are tariffs on Chinese quartz turning into orders, and when will the loan-to-equity conversion be complete?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Chinese quartz tariffs have had no impact on revenue and Section 201 duties are paid by customers. Majority of loan already converted; process takes 2-3 months with immediate financial effect.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise about Rs 17 crore since March, and when will collections normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Dispatches were disrupted in March and May due to geopolitics; dispatches resumed from UAE after late May. Receivable turnaround is 90-150 days, so receivables expected to normalise towards end of Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much H1 operating cash flow came from higher payables, and what is the H2 debt reduction plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave an approximate figure of 70-75% of H1 (stated as H1 revenue) from higher payables, caveated as an assumption-based estimate; no debt reduction plan was given in the answer.

qa_highlights.question: Are forex gains likely to reverse and how is currency risk hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 FX gain was due to rupee depreciation from about 90 to 96; dollar-rupee now near same level. Packing credits are taken in foreign currency and future orders are hedged.

qa_highlights.question: Why was tax paid in H1 despite a loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tax was due to other income accumulation; standalone entity made a profit, so tax was payable.

capex_capacity: Two engineered stone plants: Mahindra World City SEZ (Jaipur) and Global Surfaces FZE at Jebel Ali (Dubai); combined annual production about 1.14 million sq m.
H1 volumes described by an analyst as about one-third of annual capacity; management did not give a figure but said utilisation is low and would improve once geopolitical situation stabilises.
Management said raw material disruptions in H1 caused production breakdowns; Marquartz volumes cannot grow currently due to raw material shortages.
Domestic brand launch via dealer network planned this quarter; domestic dispatches from November 2026; about 70% of domestic-product output from India plant and 30-35% from UAE.
Bagru natural stone unit discontinued effective 31 March 2026; only limited activity to complete existing orders and orderly closure.
demand_pricing: US Section 201 safeguard on quartz surface products effective 15 August 2026 for 4 years via a single global tariff-rate quota: additional 25% duty on about 13 million sq m in year one, 50% above quota; rates taper to 19%-47% by year four. India and UAE not exempted.
Management said quartz surface exports to US were about 223 million (unit as stated) in 2026, about 72% of India's total quartz exports (industry estimate).

Pricing: raw material prices rose 25-50%, implying about 10% estimated average impact on selling prices, but company has not passed on major increases; only part of freight cost passed on via FOB pricing.
Freight on imported raw materials rose nearly five-fold.
Export about 96% and domestic about 4% of revenue; engineered stone about 98% of H1 revenue.
Marquartz (licensed, patented vein process) average selling price about 20-30% above regular products; competition lower given patent; utilisation similar to group average.
Management said Chinese quartz tariffs have had no impact on company revenue; Section 201 duties are paid by customers.
risks_watch: US Section 201 quartz safeguard (from 15 August 2026) and India's unresolved trade status: WTO consultations requested; India-US interim trade framework unsigned.
Raw material cost and freight spikes tied to regional geopolitics (petroleum above $110 per management) and raw material supply disruptions causing production breakdowns.
Margin recovery to ~12% uncertain; management said it cannot confirm if conditions persist.
Receivables build-up of about Rs 17 crore since March; normalisation expected towards end Q3 FY27 (90-150 day cycle).
UAE segment loss figures (analyst cited about Rs 57 million in Q2 vs Rs 31 million in Q1) unconfirmed by management; other income fell sharply from Rs 9.4 crore to Rs 1.8 crore in H1.
Domestic brand launch and India dispatches from November 2026; success vs. 70% India / 30-35% UAE output split to be tracked.

adds.what: Domestic brand launch via dealer network with dispatches from India plant (Mahindra World City SEZ) from Nov 2026; not a new plant

growth.why: Management guides revenue run-rate of Rs 70-80 crore per quarter, realistically by Q4 FY27 and dependent on geopolitics, but backing is vague: utilisation is low (H1 volume about one-third of annual capacity), raw material supply disrupted, and no new capacity is being added.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 2.17% from 12.69% in Q1 on raw material costs up 25-50% and freight up nearly 5x, and management cannot say whether margin returns to ~12% if conditions persist; costs are expected to normalise within 1-2 months only if geopolitics stabilise.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant is discussed; the existing two plants (about 1.14 million sq m combined) run at roughly one-third utilisation in H1, and the Bagru natural stone unit is being discontinued from 31 March 2026.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets a Rs 70-80 crore quarterly revenue run-rate realistically by Q4 FY27 versus Rs 60 crore in Q2 (+10.7% YoY), but it is conditional on geopolitics and raw material supply, which caused production breakdowns in H1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is low (H1 volume about one-third of capacity) and no new capex is discussed, so a fresh capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management described the near-term operating environment as remaining challenging given US Section 201 duties from 15 August 2026 and regional geopolitics; H1 revenue fell 2.6% YoY to Rs 125 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 loss after tax of Rs 5.3 crore, Q2 EBITDA margin of 2.17%, receivables up about Rs 17 crore since March, and Section 201 duties from 15 August 2026 leave execution risk if geopolitics do not stabilise.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Domestic brand launch via dealer network is planned this quarter with India dispatches from November 2026, with about 70% of domestic output from the India plant and 30-35% from UAE.

rows.label: Price increases not yet taken
rows.why: Raw material prices rose 25-50%, implying about 10% impact on selling prices, but the company has not passed on major increases; any hike depends on geopolitics and market acceptance.

rows.label: Receivables normalisation
rows.why: Receivables rose about Rs 17 crore since March; with a 90-150 day turnaround, management expects normalisation towards end Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Loan to UAE FZE equity conversion
rows.why: Approval is done for converting the Rs 110-111 crore loan to FZE equity; the process takes 2-3 months with immediate financial effect per management.

tone.note: Management was constructive on cost normalisation and the domestic launch but cautious and defensive on margins, pricing and the 12% margin target, tying everything to geopolitical stabilisation; analysts pressed on UAE losses, utilisation thresholds, cash flow from payables and the path to Rs 70-80
